Here’s a straight‐up comparison between **Intel 13th-Gen i5 vs 13th-Gen i7** — what you gain, what you pay for, and when it makes sense. If you want, I can break it down by desktop vs laptop variants too.

---

## What they are / what “i5 vs i7” means (13th gen)

- Both belong to Intel’s *Raptor Lake* family. Same architecture, same socket (LGA1700 for desktops). citeturn0search2turn0search3turn0search7  
- Differences come down to **core count (performance + efficiency cores), threads, clock speeds (base / turbo), cache**, and **power draw / thermal requirements**. citeturn0search2turn0search7turn0search8turn0search3

---

## Key specs comparison (a typical pair: e.g. i5-13600K vs i7-13700K)

| Spec | i5-13600K | i7-13700K |
|---|---|---|
| P-(Performance) cores | 6 | 8 citeturn0search2turn0search3turn0search7 |
| E-(Efficiency) cores | 8 | 8 citeturn0search2turn0search7 |
| Threads | 20 | 24 citeturn0search2turn0search7 |
| Max Turbo P-core clock | ~5.1 GHz | ~5.4 GHz citeturn0search2turn0search3turn0search7 |
| Cache (Smart Cache / L2 etc.) | less (≈ 24 MB) | more (≈ 30 MB) citeturn0search7 |
| Power / Thermal demand | Lower (still high for “K” variants) | Higher citeturn0search10turn0search2turn0search7 |

---

## What that means in practice

### Pros of going with i7 over i5

- **Better multi-threaded performance** — more P-cores + higher turbo speeds + larger cache helps in tasks like video editing, 3D rendering, software compiling.  
- **Slight edge in single-threaded or lightly threaded tasks** because of higher clocks.  
- Futureproofing: more headroom for heavier workloads.  

### Downsides / trade-offs

- **Higher power draw / heat**. The i7 “K” models pull significantly more wattage than i5. You’ll need better cooling, possibly a more robust power supply. citeturn0search10turn0search7  
- **Less cost-efficient for gaming or general usage**: If your tasks are mostly gaming or light work, an i5 might give you nearly as much performance per rupee, because in many games the GPU becomes the bottleneck, and the i7’s extra threads or cores won’t matter as much.  
- **Marginal gains in some use-cases**: In gaming, particularly at higher resolutions, the difference may be small. citeturn0search10  

---

## When i5 is “good enough”

- If you’re building a gaming PC where GPU is more critical.  
- If your workload is moderate: web dev, office work, light video/photo editing.  
- If you have constraints on budget, power, or cooling.  
- If you don’t mind upgrading in a few years rather than having top performance now.

---

## My direct take: what I'd pick and when

If I were you and had a moderate budget, I’d probably go with a good 13th-gen i5 (e.g. 13600K or non-K if power is a concern). You get *most* of the performance for a much better price/efficiency. Only if I were doing heavy productivity work that really uses many cores/threads (video editing, virtualization, etc.) would I push for the i7.

---

If you tell me **which specific models** (desktop or laptop, your budget, what you’ll use it for: gaming / editing / streaming etc.), I can tell you whether going for an i7 is worth the extra cost *for your use*. Do you want me to compare a few options for you?
I5 has more course then i7

Not true — in **13th gen**, the **i7 actually has more cores than the i5**.  

Here’s how it breaks down (desktop versions, since those are the most common for this comparison):

- **i5-13600K** → **14 cores total** (6 Performance + 8 Efficiency) → 20 threads.  
- **i7-13700K** → **16 cores total** (8 Performance + 8 Efficiency) → 24 threads.  

👉 So the i7 has **2 more P-cores** and **4 more threads** than the i5.  

If you’re looking at laptop versions, the story is similar: i7 models usually come with higher core counts and higher clocks than i5.  

Do you want me to break it down for **laptop CPUs** too (like i5-13500H vs i7-13700H), or are you only asking about **desktop chips**?

Here’s a detailed breakdown of how **i5-13500H vs i7-13620H** compare — what each is good/bad at, and whether upgrading to the i7 is really worth it **for you**.

---

## Spec comparison

| Spec | **i5-13500H** | **i7-13620H** |
|---|---|---|
| P-cores (Performance cores) | 4 citeturn0search4turn0search14turn0search21 | 6 citeturn0search6turn0search12turn0search0turn0search19 |
| E-cores (Efficiency cores) | 8 citeturn0search4turn0search21turn0search14 | 4 citeturn0search6turn0search12turn0search19turn0search0 |
| Total cores / threads | 12 cores / 16 threads citeturn0search21turn0search4turn0search14 | 10 cores / 16 threads citeturn0search6turn0search12turn0search19 |
| Base / Boost P-core clock | ~2.6 GHz base, ~4.7 GHz boost citeturn0search4turn0search21 | ~2.4 GHz base, ~4.9 GHz boost citeturn0search12turn0search0turn0search6 |
| E-core clock | ~1.9 GHz base, ~3.5 GHz boost citeturn0search21turn0search4turn0search14 | ~1.8 GHz base, ~3.6 GHz boost citeturn0search6turn0search12 |
| Cache (L3) | 18 MB citeturn0search4turn0search21turn0search14 | 24 MB citeturn0search12turn0search6turn0search19 |
| Power / TDP | ≈ 35-45 W (PL1) to ~115 W (turbo) citeturn0search4turn0search14turn0search10 | ≈ 45 W base, up to PL2 ~115 W under load citeturn0search12turn0search6turn0search0 |

---

## What this means in real performance

- **Single-threaded / light tasks**: i7-13620H has slightly better peak performance (higher P-core boost, more raw P-cores) so for stuff like launching apps, lighter gaming, etc., you’ll see a modest gain. citeturn0search9turn0search6turn0search0  
- **Multi-thread / heavy multitasking**: i5-13500H has more *total cores* (because of more E-cores), so in workloads that can use all cores (video encoding, rendering, multitasking), i5 may sometimes be closer or even beat the i7 in some scenarios. But i7 still tends to win on tasks that rely heavily on P-cores. citeturn0search21turn0search9turn0search0turn0search6  
- **Power & heat**: The i7 draws more when boosting, so in thin laptops or under sustained load, it may hit thermal limits or throttle more. The i5, with more E-cores and fewer P-cores, might be more efficient in those cases. citeturn0search6turn0search21turn0search4  
- **Graphics (integrated)**: i5-13500H uses a stronger iGPU (Iris Xe 80 EU) vs i7-13620H (UHD Graphics 64 EU) in many reps. So if you rely on integrated GPU for tasks, i5 might even win in graphics. citeturn0reddit46turn0search14turn0search0  

---

## Benchmarks / numbers

- In multi-threaded benchmarks, i7-13620H is about **~13% faster** than i5-13500H. citeturn0search1turn0search9  
- In single-threaded, the i7 is only **~5-6% faster** than i5. citeturn0search1turn0search9  

---

## So, is the i7 worth it for *you*?

Here’s my honest take (no sugarcoating):

- If your work involves heavily multi-core tasks (video editing, streaming + gaming, compiling code, VMs, etc.) then yes, i7 gives enough boost to make a difference. The gains are real but not massive.

- But if your usage is mostly gaming, normal productivity (office, browsing, coding lightly), watching videos, etc., then the i5-13500H gives *very good performance*, and you might not notice much difference in everyday use. The extra cost / heat / battery impact of going to i7 might *not* be worth it.

- Also, in laptops the cooling solution matters a lot. If the laptop with i7 has weaker cooling, it'll throttle and reduce the advantage.

---

If you tell me your **budget difference** between the two, and what you’ll mainly do (gaming / editing / battery life / portability etc.), I can tell you whether I’d go for i7 or just settle with i5 (for *you*). Do you want me to do that?
